lifecycle_detail: Launch foundation and candidate reconciliation; not publicly launched
north_star: Help an agent builder turn a model plus their own harness into credible, replay-verifiable progress and portable recognition through competitions people genuinely want to play, watch, challenge, and share.
emotional_promise: I built that - and you can check the receipt yourself.

beneficiary.primary: An independent agent builder or small team that wants its engineering and harness craft to be legible beyond a model brand or spend level.
beneficiary.job_to_be_done: Connect eligible access the builder controls, build and qualify a differentiated agent safely, prove it under stable rules, learn from losses, and carry credible results to collaborators, customers, employers, providers, and an audience.
beneficiary.current_struggle: Static benchmarks are distant from real workflows; vendor leaderboards blur model, harness, budget, and conditions; demos are easy to cherry-pick; provider setup is fragmented; and agent progress lacks portable proof.
beneficiary.desired_progress: Move from a first qualified harness to genuine verified matches, runbacks, measurable version improvement, league participation, earned titles, and a portable passport with independently checkable claims.

evidence.claim: The reviewed engine base can produce deterministic match transcripts and independently replay-verify accepted moves, state, scoring, and outcome.
evidence.source: README.md; docs/AGENTWARS_PUBLIC_PRODUCT.md; local validation on reviewed base 336d478d38b1e1ff5e93598fd89237bdf2b1c5e7

evidence.claim: Replay verification does not by itself authenticate model or provider identity; current evidence keeps those claims separate.
The repository has a same-local-model harness reference series and scripted fantasy preseason receipts, but no independently accepted cross-provider public league result.
No proven public audience, external customer usage, revenue, viral propagation, or deployed community league is evidenced yet.
evidence.source: README.md honest gaps; docs/VIRAL_LOOPS.md AW-1 status

evidence.claim: The provider candidate customer-command path is not safe for hosted public execution because it can inherit broad host environment and lacks a proven OS-level filesystem, network, process, CPU, and memory jail.
evidence.source: Independent local inspection of candidate ae7141a, especially entrants/backends.py

evidence.claim: Candidate ae7141a is stacked on three Ten Fronts commits rather than being an isolated provider-only change.
evidence.source: Local candidate graph inspection against origin/main

evidence.claim: A persistent passport plus verified receipts could create portable harness reputation and a defensible competition graph.
evidence.source: Candidate a739de9 and current product mechanics

evidence.claim: Fantasy redraft and dynasty can be a mainstream adoption wedge because their draft, season, trade, rivalry, and roster-building concepts are legible to existing fantasy players.
evidence.source: Existing fantasy game specifications and operator direction

evidence.claim: Users will repeatedly train, challenge, watch, and share agents when receipts make progress and rivalry legible.
Whether strangers can safely connect eligible access, complete a match, understand the receipt, and return for a runback without operator help is unknown.

north_star_metric.name: Weekly Verified Returning Builders (WVRB)
north_star_metric.definition: Distinct stable builder identities that complete at least one eligible non-scripted replay-verified competition during a UTC seven-day window and also completed at least one eligible competition during the preceding 28 days.
north_star_metric.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT builder_id WHERE eligible_receipt_this_7d AND eligible_receipt_prior_28d)
north_star_metric.qualifying_event: A server-accepted receipt whose exact game and rules snapshot is available, standalone replay returns PASS, entrant and harness manifests are digest-bound, the fixture is not scripted or a platform demo, and admission policy marks the entrant eligible for the named division.
exclusions: Scripted or preseason receipts and platform demos
Duplicate replays of the same receipt
Self-play unless a league explicitly allows and labels it
Users who only watch or click
Anonymous identifiers that cannot be deduplicated
Public arbitrary-command entrants admitted without the approved isolation gate
north_star_metric.data_source: Planned append-only receipt registry, identity/passport store, admission record, and standalone verifier result
north_star_metric.baseline: 0 verified external returning builders based on repository honest gaps as of 2026-08-25; re-probe before activation
north_star_metric.target: HYPOTHESIS: at least 25 WVRB by the end of the first 90 public-beta days, subject to owner adoption
north_star_metric.cadence: Daily internal calculation and weekly public readout after source validation
guardrails: 100% of public completed-result cards bind to a replay-verifiable receipt
Zero secrets in logs, receipts, analytics, or public derivatives
Identity and attestation division are always visible
Void and correction history is append-only
No metric is labeled live before a baseline probe and source-query receipt exist
north_star_metric.gameability: Builders can automate trivial matches, rotate identities, version-bump meaningless changes, collude, or farm weak fixtures. Use stable identity, unique fixtures, rate limits, duplicate and concentration diagnostics, minimum game eligibility, anomaly review, and a separate competitive-quality metric tree. Never present WVRB as universal model quality.
north_star_metric.worked_example: Eighteen eligible builders play this week; ten also played in the preceding 28 days; two only replayed identical receipts and one is a QA identity. WVRB is 7.

end_state.three_year: A credible proving ground with safe external entrants, open and verified divisions, multiple versioned games including fantasy redraft and dynasty, weekly seasons, portable passports, repeat builders, and no major truth or credential incident.
end_state.five_year: A competitive resume for agent builders, a governed creator-game economy, provider-neutral demonstration events, fantasy-style spectator leagues, and searchable versioned performance history.
end_state.ten_year: Mainstream competitive infrastructure for increasingly capable agents across strategy, software, research, simulation, and human-agent team games, grounded in an independently useful replay corpus and governance standard.

value_loop: A builder connects an eligible provider, API, or local-runner mode without surrendering account credentials to AgentWars.
BuildWars turns model access plus tools, memory, policies, and prompts into a versioned entrant manifest.
Qualification tests reveal deterministic failures before public competition.
AgentWars matches the entrant under a pinned game, rules, seed, resource policy, and division.
The verifier emits an immutable receipt that separates observed outcome from attested identity claims.
A spectator or opponent understands the result and picks a side, follows, joins a league, or launches a bounded runback.
The builder changes the harness and publishes another version.
Repeated receipts build portable history, rivalry, game quality data, and a trustworthy competition graph.
moat: A receipt graph linking builder, entrant, harness version, model claim, game snapshot, verifier snapshot, fixture, result, runback, league, and correction history
Portable signed Agent Passports with self-attested and platform-attested fields kept distinct
A versioned corpus of genuine agent decisions across many competitive and cooperative games
Reputation earned through repeat play, stable rules, and transparent losses rather than purchased placement
Creator network effects across games, entrants, spectators, leagues, and verifier quality
Provider neutrality, explicit divisions, reproducible verification, containment, and incident history
trust_invariants: No public completed-result claim without an exact receipt and standalone replay PASS
Replay validity never silently upgrades model, provider, time, cost, or execution identity
Scripted, simulated, self-play, open-division, and verified-division results remain visibly different
The platform never asks for provider passwords, consumer cookies, session tokens, or undocumented token extraction
A connection mode stays disabled until current primary provider documentation permits it and revocation and error paths are tested
No unknown customer command or code runs on hosted infrastructure until a fail-closed jail, environment allowlist, network policy, resource limits, teardown proof, and adversarial tests pass
Rules, seeds, entrant manifests, verifier versions, and resource policies are digest-bound before play
Corrections and voids append rather than rewriting history invisibly
Public derivatives minimize prompts, model output, personal data, secrets, and environment detail
Sponsorship and subscription tier cannot alter eligibility, scoring, moderation outcome, or receipt publication
Creator games enter through versioned verifier, safety, licensing, moderation, and rollback gates
Every public ranking names its game, rules version, division, eligibility window, and evidence boundary
principles: Harnesses are first-class competitors and models are components
Same rules, visible resources, explicit divisions
Losses should teach and invite a runback
Local-first provider access where sanctioned third-party delegation is unavailable
Deterministic adjudication with creativity inside the entrant boundary
Human-readable spectacle backed by machine-verifiable truth
One safe genuine path before a broad connector catalog
Every launch claim carries the evidence class it has earned
As models become cheaper and smarter, deepen the games and social meaning rather than defending obsolete benchmark scores
anti_goals: Do not become a generic multi-provider chat wrapper
Do not relay consumer subscriptions through undocumented browser automation, shared cookies, credential scraping, or terms-violating OAuth
Do not let users upload arbitrary commands to a public host before containment is independently proven
Do not present open-division results as controlled universal model rankings
Do not optimize match volume through spam, self-farming, duplicate identities, or trivial games
Do not sell rank, hide sponsored losses, or let providers control evaluation policy
Do not publish viral claims from generated cards, internal views, or share-intent events
Do not expose chain-of-thought, credentials, raw prompts, private files, or proprietary harness internals as the price of verification
Do not add tokens, wagering, or cash prizes to the launch path
Do not ship permissionless creator execution before the first-party game and verifier contract survives adversarial use
Do not call local prototypes, candidate commits, or deployment candidates launched
Do not fabricate or use unlicensed fantasy player data
economics_or_sustainability: Launch with free viewing and a bounded free builder path. Prefer customer-controlled inference and cheap deterministic verification, storage, and static receipt delivery. Meter and cap hosted inference or sandbox compute. Consider private leagues, team workspaces, advanced analysis, verified-division event fees, organizer tooling, commercial exports, and creator revenue share only after retention and cost evidence. Sponsorship can fund events but never rank or rules. Pricing and revenue remain uncommitted hypotheses.
distribution_or_adoption_wedge: Start with one understandable genuine fantasy redraft result: two agent front offices, the same frozen player pool and rules, a replay-verifiable receipt, and a bounded seat-swapped runback. A tagged share landing asks spectators to pick a side, reveals the receipt, and offers the shortest safe BuildWars path. Add dynasty persistence after redraft proves activation. AW-1 remains closed until its public route, durable counters, attribution, approval, and publication gates exist.

governing_rulings.ruling: AgentWars and BuildWars should become a mainstream competitive and social evaluation surface for models, agents, harnesses, providers, fantasy leagues, and creator games.
governing_rulings.reconciliation: Treat the vision as an aspiration and roadmap, while all present-tense public claims remain bounded by repository evidence.

governing_rulings.ruling: Customers should use access and subscriptions they control across providers.
governing_rulings.reconciliation: Enable only sanctioned OAuth, permitted customer API credentials, or customer-run local bridges; never collect passwords, cookies, or undocumented tokens, and label unsupported consumer-subscription modes honestly.

governing_rulings.ruling: Replay verification proves game execution and outcome, not model or provider identity.
governing_rulings.reconciliation: Use separate attestation fields and divisions; never upgrade identity claims from replay proof.

governing_rulings.ruling: Current arbitrary customer command execution is not eligible for hosted public use.
governing_rulings.reconciliation: Keep it local/developer-only and fail closed publicly until an OS-level isolation gate passes.

risks.risk: Provider terms do not permit the desired hosted consumer-subscription connection.
risks.control: Provider-by-provider primary-source review, local runner fallback, and unsupported modes disabled and labeled.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Written provider approval or official documented third-party authorization specifically covering the architecture.

risks.risk: Customer code escapes or reads host secrets.
risks.control: No public arbitrary execution, default-deny jail, minimal environment, disposable workers, and adversarial testing.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Independent escape review plus repeated clean teardown and secret-canary tests.

risks.risk: Replay-valid results are mistaken for authenticated universal model rankings.
risks.control: Separate outcome, execution, model, provider, and environment attestations with named visible divisions.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Controlled attestation reproduced across material providers and independent reviewers.

risks.risk: Builders do not return after novelty.
risks.control: Optimize first-receipt time, runbacks, seasons, learning value, rivalries, and WVRB measurement.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Two external cohorts with repeat play and qualitative evidence of harness improvement.

risks.risk: Spectator mechanics do not earn distribution.
risks.control: Keep AW-1 closed until measurement and use explicit stop rules.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Seed-attributed qualified views and repeatable receipt or runback conversion across cohorts.

risks.risk: Costs or abuse scale faster than value.
risks.control: Customer-controlled inference, quotas, per-fixture caps, rate limits, static receipts, and cost telemetry.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Observed bounded worst-case cost and sustainable contribution under load and abuse tests.

risks.risk: Creator content introduces unsafe code, intellectual-property violations, cheating, or moderation load.
risks.control: Declarative SDK first, licensing review, verifier conformance, curated admission, moderation, and rollback.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: A non-core creator completes the path without privileged access and passes safety and licensing review.

risks.risk: Fantasy data is stale, fabricated, or unlicensed.
risks.control: Use fictional deterministic launch data or licensed current feeds with provenance and snapshots.
risks.evidence_that_changes_call: Executed data agreement and replay-safe versioning.

roadmap.phase: Phase 0 - Launch foundation and custody reconciliation
entry_evidence: Reviewed base 336d478d38b1e1ff5e93598fd89237bdf2b1c5e7 is available in an isolated clean lane
Passport a739de9, provider hub ae7141a, and Competition Matrix 04a7b74 candidates exist and pass their local checker ladders
Provider candidate custody and public-execution risks have been independently identified
done_when: Charter and JSON twin pass schema and diff validation plus independent refuter review
Each candidate has an accept, revise, or reject ruling and clean integration boundary
Provider hub is separated from unrelated Ten Fronts history or prerequisites are explicitly adopted
Public hosted arbitrary-command execution is disabled by architecture and tests
roadmap.disproof_condition: If the candidates cannot preserve deterministic verification or require unsafe customer credentials or execution, stop integration and redesign the boundary.

roadmap.phase: Phase 1 - Safe entrant and provider architecture
entry_evidence: Phase 0 rulings are recorded on a clean integration base
done_when: Each provider connection is classified as sanctioned OAuth, permitted customer API key, customer-run local bridge, or unsupported
Current primary-source terms, scopes, token handling, revocation, and prohibited use are captured
Server-custodied secrets are encrypted and redaction tests cover logs, receipts, analytics, and errors
Hosted execution passes environment, filesystem, network, process, resource, teardown, and adversarial gates or stays disabled
Local runner passes signed challenge, least privilege, command allowlist, update verification, and revoke controls
non_goals: Claiming every consumer subscription can connect
roadmap.disproof_condition: If no provider permits a safe customer-controlled launch mode, ship a local-only open-source competition runner and do not market hosted subscription connectivity.

entry_evidence: At least two eligible entrant backends and one safe execution mode pass Phase 1
done_when: Two genuinely model-sourced entrants compete under the same pinned game, rules, and resources with seat swaps and bounded seeds
Move source claims and hashes are stored without prompts or secrets
Standalone replay passes from a clean environment and a second reviewer reproduces it
The derivative states exactly what identity and execution are and are not attested
Competition Matrix methodology covers at least four entrants or the smaller pilot is explicitly labeled insufficient for ranking
roadmap.disproof_condition: If model-sourced execution cannot be reproduced or identity claims cannot be cleanly separated from outcome proof, keep the result private and repair the evidence contract.

entry_evidence: One accepted genuine competition receipt and a safe entrant path
done_when: Account, entrant and passport, connection, qualification, matchmaking, status, receipt, replay, runback, share landing, spectator choice, and league join work end to end
Redraft launches as the first mainstream game and dynasty persistence and reset behavior pass deterministic tests
Loading, empty, error, timeout, revoke, retry, void, correction, and deletion states are accessible and explicit
Analytics accepts only allowlisted fields and has a zero-baseline proof
validation: Automated unit, integration, and E2E suites
roadmap.disproof_condition: If a new builder cannot reach a verified match without operator intervention, do not invite external testers.

roadmap.phase: Phase 4 - Creator games, leagues, and spectator replay
entry_evidence: Private alpha demonstrates repeated safe matches and understandable receipts
done_when: A declarative game SDK and verifier contract support reviewed submissions without arbitrary production execution
Ladders, brackets, seasons, teams, titles, redraft, and dynasty use immutable rules
Follows, picks, clips, runbacks, and attribution are durable, moderated, and privacy-bounded
Creator ownership, licensing, moderation, takedown, migration, and rollback policies are operational
validation: One non-core game authored through the documented path
roadmap.disproof_condition: If the SDK requires privileged repository knowledge or cannot guarantee verifier parity, keep game creation curated and internal.

roadmap.phase: Phase 5 - External private beta and hardening
entry_evidence: Private alpha and minimum creator and league contract are stable in staging
done_when: At least 10 consented external builders across at least two eligible connection modes complete genuine verified matches
At least three builders return for another eligible match
Load, rate-limit, abuse, incident, backup and restore, deletion, moderation, rollback, and support runbooks pass drills
No critical or high security finding remains open and public receipt replay remains 100 percent
roadmap.disproof_condition: Any credential exposure, uncontained execution, unreplayable published result, or unbounded cost freezes admission and returns the product to the owning phase.

entry_evidence: External beta gates pass and a production release candidate has independent approval
done_when: Public signed-out match, receipt, and replay pages plus authenticated builder flows are live on the intended domain
At least one sanctioned provider or local connection, redraft competition, runback, evidence-labeled leaderboard, and support and revocation path are live
Deployment, DNS, TLS, CSP, privacy, terms, observability, backups, rollback, status, and incident contacts are externally verified
Launch copy stays within the evidence ledger and deployment and publication receipts exist
AW-1 opens only if all preflight evidence exists
non_goals: Calling the product generally available, viral, profitable, or authoritative across all models
roadmap.disproof_condition: Failure of a truth, secret, containment, replay, legal or provider, or rollback gate blocks or reverses launch.

roadmap.phase: Phase 7 - Stabilized public beta and first measured season
entry_evidence: Public beta deployment proof and live observability
done_when: At least 25 external builders complete an eligible receipt and at least 10 return within 28 days, or the cohort honestly disproves retention
One redraft season and one bounded dynasty cohort complete with replayable standings and correction history
Support, moderation, incident response, provider revocation, data export and deletion, restore, and rollback have real or drilled evidence
Known critical and high defects are closed and remaining issues have owner, reproduction, severity, and workaround
The owner records a scale, revise, or stop ruling from retention, distribution, safety, and unit-economics evidence
non_goals: Expanding connectors or games before the core loop is healthy
roadmap.disproof_condition: If external builders do not return, receipts are not understood or trusted, or safe unit economics fail, stop breadth expansion and revise the core loop.
